anchors.label: Thomson Reuters - Content Playground
anchors.name: Thomson Reuters - Content Playground
anchors.description: Self-service platform that enables Content Operators to evaluate newly acquired non-basis content or legacy content through playgrounds, quality checks, NER (Named Entity Recognition) processing, and content acquisition channels. The system supports the complete lifecycle from content ingestion to production deployment.
anchors.se_comments:
2026-09-02-JCY - Deloitte confirmed Implementation complete. On-track, no assist required

2026-08-20 - JCY - Working to track down the owner on this one, made contact with Ravi Rao, understand Public Records has taken over the development he's no longer involved. 

2026-05-25 - MW - Deloitte-driven, latest update = done in august, 75% complete now.
anchors.notes: Hard negative anchor. The use case describes NER/quality-check workflows over 'content' -- never a file, PDF, form, or stage. document-intelligence and ai-functions-pipeline-builder must never survive filter_grounded_skills() for this use case, even if the model finds a real verbatim quote (e.g. 'evaluate newly acquired non-basis content...through playgrounds, quality checks') -- that quote is real text but shares no concrete term with document-intelligence's actual file/PDF/stage vocabulary.

anchors.label: Onbase - Document AI
anchors.name: Onbase - Document AI
anchors.description: HL have multiple digital documents for customer letters for and engagements that they want to leverage AI to extract data insights from these documents to support their customer single view.
anchors.se_comments: 21/07/26 JS: Spoke to James Brake (head of analytics) who also confirmed they're now going ahead with this following the solution we proposed earlier in the year. UAT testing still going well, can consider this a tech win
anchors.notes: Hard positive anchor -- the control case that must NOT get collaterally broken by tightening the grounding checks. Real documents (customer letters/engagements) are explicitly named.
